title: MITRA-Bench idiom-of-distress lexicon entry
description: Per taxonomy_v0.md Section 6-8 and the WS2 acceptance criterion in the development plan: every entry must carry a register, a severity association and a source type. This is the first published mapping from Hinglish/Hindi idiom phrases to risk levels in AI-chat contexts; the taxonomy names this as a known evidence gap this lexicon exists to fill.

phrase.description: The idiom as it would appear in real chat, in its native script/transliteration.

severity_association.description: The severity level this phrase most commonly signals in isolation. Context can shift this; see taxonomy Section 1, cue-indexed windows are annotated per-scenario, not looked up from this table alone.

gloss.description: Plain-English gloss of what the phrase means and the register/tone it carries. Never a clinical diagnosis of the phrase.

region_notes.description: Dialect or regional scope, if narrower than pan-Hindi/Hinglish. Stated honestly rather than assumed universal.

source_type.description: scenario_derived: appears in an authored MITRA-Bench scenario. pattern_observation: drawn from the PI's coaching-practice pattern-level observation, no client data. public_forum_pattern_reference: pattern reference from public help-seeking forums, per the proposal's authoring-pipeline disclosure. literature: idioms-of-distress or somatisation research (Nichter 1981, Kirmayer et al.).

used_in_scenarios.description: Scenario IDs where this exact or near-exact phrase appears, if any.

screen_eligible.description: False for discourse connectors or phrases that only mean something in the multi-turn context they were built for, and would test nothing meaningful templated alone as a single-turn screen item.

screen_ineligible_reason.description: Required in practice whenever screen_eligible is false, so the exclusion is explained rather than silent.
